Effervescent

ef-er-VES-ent · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Effervescent is high-spirited or enthusiastic.

The new intern's effervescent personality made her an instant favorite around the office.

Worked Example

The effervescent tour guide kept the entire group laughing and engaged for six straight hours.

Effervescent describes a bubbly, sparkling social charm -- literally, the same word used for a fizzy drink.

How Effervescent Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

bubbly

bubbly: showing high spirits or lively energy

sparkling

sparkling: radiating lively charm

Antonyms

gloomy

gloomy: showing sadness or low spirits

lifeless

lifeless: lacking energy or vitality

How Strong Is It? — pleasant → electrifying → effervescent

pleasant vs. effervescent

pleasant vs. effervescent: Being pleasant is mild and easy; being effervescent means visibly sparkling with energy in a room.

electrifying vs. effervescent

electrifying vs. effervescent: Electrifying describes an energy so intense it charges an entire crowd, beyond simply being effervescent.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of effervescent.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — ef-

prefix — ef-: out (variant of ex-) (Latin)

root — ferv

root — ferv: to boil, to glow (Latin (fervere))

suffix — -escent

suffix — -escent: becoming, in the process of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: ef- ("out") + ferv ("to boil, glow") + -escent ("becoming") = bubbling out, like a fizzy drink.

Use the root in a new word: fervent

Use the root in a new word: fervent: This word shares its Latin root (fervere, "to boil, glow") with Fervent, a word you already met earlier in this course (Part 2, this same theme's own second installment) -- both come from the idea of boiling, bubbling energy.
